original_value: Continuous-valued deep convolutional networks (DNNs) can be converted into accurate rate-coding based spike neural networks (SNNs). However, the substantial computational and energy costs, which is caused by multiple spikes, limit their use in mobile and embedded applications. And recent works have shown that the newly emerged temporal-coding based SNNs converted from DNNs can reduce the computational load effectively. In this paper, we propose a novel method to convert DNNs to temporal-coding SNNs, called TDSNN. Combined with the characteristic of the leaky integrate-andfire (LIF) neural model, we put forward a new coding principle Reverse Coding and design a novel Ticking Neuron mechanism. According to our evaluation, our proposed method achieves 42% total operations reduction on average in large networks comparing with DNNs with no more than 0.5% accuracy loss. The evaluation shows that TDSNN may prove to be one of the key enablers to make the adoption of SNNs widespread.

result.paraphrase: Continuous-valued deep convolutional networks (DNNs) can be transformed into accurate rate-coding spike neural networks (SNNs). However, their extensive computational and energy overhead, caused by multiple spikes, limits applicability in mobile and embedded settings. Recent studies have also shown that newly developed temporal-coding SNNs converted from DNNs can effectively reduce computational load. In this paper, we introduce TDSNN, a novel method for converting DNNs to temporal-coding SNNs. Leveraging the leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron model, we propose a new coding principle called Reverse Coding and develop a novel Ticking Neuron mechanism. Our evaluation indicates that the proposed method reduces total operations by 42% on average in large networks compared with DNNs, while incurring no more than 0.5% accuracy loss. The results suggest that TDSNN could be a key enabler for broader adoption of SNNs.
